title: Fresh Start Career Roadmap: SAP Finance Edition
subtitle: Tuesday 17 November 2026 – Sunday 31 January 2027 · follow the order, not the dates
bottomLine: A fresh start on Tuesday 17 November. One plan, all areas moving every week, for about 8.3 hours of study a week, plus about 4 hours of exercise, recovery, family time and daily practice. Weekdays are about 45–55 minutes; Saturday about 2 hours; Sunday about 2½ hours. Busy go-live week? Switch to the reduced routine. Follow the order, not the dates. A missed day moves the next task one slot later; nothing is lost.

areas.name: SAP Finance
areas.objective: SAP vocabulary and processes from day one
areas.byEnd: 10 SAP Fridays; 25-term glossary quiz 20/25; P2P explained in SAP words (7/10)
areas.assessed: Tuesday flashcards: 8 of 10 without looking. Check 1: 25-term glossary quiz 20/25, and P2P explained aloud in 2 minutes, 7/10 on the rubric
areas.success: 10 SAP Fridays; glossary quiz 20/25; P2P explained in SAP words (7/10)
areas.stretch: Explain O2C and data migration in SAP words too
rules: Every Friday evening (40 min): one SAP topic from the free learning journeys on learning.sap.com, mapped to what you already do in your current ERP.
Add 5 terms to your glossary deck every Friday. Every Tuesday (10 min): last Friday's 5 terms + 5 older ones, said aloud; missed cards go to the front.
Download the next week's SAP pages during Sunday's review, so poor internet never blocks Friday.
Fri 25 Dec is a rest day, so there is no SAP Friday in week 6.

areas.name: Accounting
areas.byEnd: NPTEL 1.2 to 3.8; journal and ledger; test #2 10/12 cold
areas.budget: 4 × 30 min, Mon–Thu (120 a week); Friday is SAP
areas.assessed: Monday cold quizzes, monthly checks and cumulative tests, with no answers in view
areas.stretch: 12/12, and you can explain each entry
rules: Watching a lecture is not mastery. Every lecture is followed by work you do before seeing the answer.
Monday starts with a cold 10-card quiz on the previous week. Mistakes become new flashcards.
Ravi Traders is your fictional business for all practice. Use made-up amounts.
Lecture numbers follow the IIT Mandi NPTEL course list. If your run differs, keep the same topic order.

areas.name: Python and AI
areas.objective: Go-live Data Kit: validator, retrieval assistant, SQL
areas.byEnd: Demo #1 and Demo #2 sent; retrieval 16/20 then 20/25; reconciliation report; template spec v0
areas.assessed: Monthly no-AI checks: functions written from a blank file and explained aloud; retrieval scored on fixed test questions
areas.notEnough: Code that runs but you can't explain
areas.success: Demo #1 and Demo #2 sent; validator finds every planted error; retrieval 16/20 then 20/25; reconciliation report
rules: Every session starts with revision (15 min Saturday, 10 min Sunday): rewrite last session's main code from memory, then compare.
Predict the output before you run anything. Type the code yourself. Stuck for 15 minutes? Ask for a hint, not the solution.
Fake data only. Save code to your private GitHub repo and to Drive after each session. Monthly checks are done with no AI.

Retrieval offline: keyword retrieval in plain Python, then TF-IDF; the answer is the top 3 chunks with their sources. Online only with a company-approved API key, kept in a .env file, never in your code.
Describe it honestly: a “retrieval assistant with sources”, not advanced AI.

areas.name: Career
areas.byEnd: Gap story; resume v0; salary targets; 4 LinkedIn conversations; role case sent
areas.assessed: Each step's “done when”; messages sent and replies
areas.success: Gap story said without notes; resume v0; salary targets; 4 conversations; role case sent
areas.stretch: Manager names clear criteria for April
rules: Keep official titles and dates; describe only what you really did. Use one calm, two-sentence answer for the gap.
Never invent SAP experience, titles or dates. Interviewers probe for it and background checks verify it.
December questions for your manager: What would I need to show to move up a level by April? Which results count most? May I publish work built only on fake data?
Check your contract before publishing anything; build on personal time and devices.
Never resign without a written offer.

areas.name: French
areas.budget: 3 × 10 min: Mon, Wed, Thu (30 a week)
areas.assessed: Thursday quizzes, both directions; the December and week-11 checks 16/20; your introduction on the rubric
rules: Monday: learn the week's 6 words and write a sentence with each.
Wednesday: say your sentences aloud 3 times, use 2 words at work, record 1 minute.
Thursday: quiz on this week's and last week's words.

areas.name: Communication
areas.byEnd: Habits most days; Sunday recordings 7/10; 2 user trainings
areas.assessed: Recordings, demos and trainings scored on the rubric (out of 10); each habit's “done when”
areas.success: Habits on most days; recordings 7/10; 2 trainings delivered
rules: Mon: speak early, one question or point in a meeting's first 10 minutes · Tue: restate one request, “So to confirm…” · Wed: same-day written summary, decided · who · by when · Thu: explain one process twice, simple then detail · Fri: concise update, done · next · blocker, under 30 seconds.
Sunday: plan 3 points (problem → what you did → result), then record 2 minutes.
Rubric targets: 6/10 or better in November–December, 7/10 or better in January.
User trainings (10–15 min) if the go-live schedule allows; otherwise the next slot. Prepare the day before.

areas.name: Evidence log
areas.byEnd: A line every day with mood; weekly go-live numbers; 3 STAR stories
areas.assessed: A line has a real result with a number, not just “worked on X”
areas.success: A line on 80% of days; weekly go-live numbers; 3 STAR stories
areas.stretch: Manager uses one of your stories
rules: One line every day with the 9 fields (date, area, task, problem, action, result, skill, evidence, lesson), plus a mood score from 1 to 5.
Every Sunday, star the best line of the week (★) and write the week's 5 go-live numbers: records loaded · rows rejected then fixed · users trained · issues closed · hours saved.
At month end, turn the starred lines into a STAR story (under 150 words): #1 Mon 30 Nov · #2 Wed 30 Dec · #3 Fri 29 Jan.

areas.name: Health · family · money · social
areas.objective: Sustainable progress and a life outside work
areas.byEnd: Sleep and exercise most days; savings automated; 3 money checks; doctor or counsellor conversation; marriage process agreed
areas.budget: Exercise 3 × 25 · alone time 2 × 15 · 60 off on Saturday · call home 25 (190 a week)
areas.assessed: Habits ticked; nights with 7 h of sleep
areas.success: Sleep 7 h most nights; exercise 2–3 times most weeks; savings automated; 3 money checks; health conversation held; marriage process agreed
areas.stretch: No week without a family call or a social contact
rules: Every day: 7 hours of sleep with a fixed lights-out time · treated water · malaria prevention · 10 minutes of daylight.

Mon · Wed · Fri: exercise 20–30 min (2 is fine in busy weeks). Tue · Thu: 10–20 minutes alone time, no screen. Wednesdays: one meal or walk with a colleague. Saturday: 60 minutes fully off. Sunday: call home, and one message or call to someone on your list of 10.

Money plan: emergency fund of 6 × your essential monthly costs, before January 2028. Automatic transfers the day after salary (from 6 Dec): one to the emergency fund, one to an exam and practice fund. Avoid rented “SAP server access” and any “placement guarantee” courses.

If low mood or poor sleep lasts more than two weeks, see a doctor or counsellor, through your company's medical contact in DRC. This is planned for 20 Dec, not left to chance. In India, Tele-MANAS is free and open 24×7: 14416 or 1-800-891-4416 (an Indian number; it may not connect from a Congolese SIM).
Protect health, sleep and family responsibilities. No streak is worth losing them.

areas.name: Daily practice
areas.objective: Calm daily rhythm and simple remedies
areas.byEnd: Morning mantra and silence most days; weekly practices kept
rules: No gemstones and no paid pujas. About 10 minutes a day (15 on Mondays).
Every morning: Om Gam Ganapataye Namah ×11 · 5 minutes of silence · one line: what you will finish today.

Mon: Om Namah Shivaya ×108; a call or message to your mother · Tue: Hanuman Chalisa; hard exercise; no angry messages · Fri: Om Shum Shukraya Namah ×27; tidy room and clothes; one small kindness · Sat: one act of service (monthly, 5 Dec and 2 Jan: a gift in kind from a small fixed budget) · Sun: feed a stray dog or birds; write 3 things that went right.
Tracked as a habit (most days), never as study time.

areas.name: Weekly review
areas.assessed: Every area has an actual result written, not just a tick
rules: Fill in the checkpoint table during the Sunday review, writing what actually happened, not just ticks.
Spending total · mood average · nights with 7 h sleep · next week's load: normal or reduced · download next week's lectures and SAP pages.

reduced.action: One line every day, with mood: busy weeks produce the best evidence
Tuesday flashcards only; Friday topic moves to next week
2 words used at work; Thursday quiz
“So to confirm…” once a day (it saves you time)
Saturday: 15-min revision + finish only the current step. Sunday off
Only fixed-date steps (manager email, December conversation); everything else waits
Sleep first; two 10-minute walks; Sunday call home
10 min Sunday: which week to repeat

recovery: Missed a day? Don't double up. Do the next task in order tomorrow.
Missed a week? Repeat the Monday quiz first, then continue where you stopped.
Two reduced weeks in a row? Shift every later date by one week. The sequence stays; only dates move.
Missing a week is fine. Don't let it become a month.
rules: Fictional data only for all practice.
Never put client names, PAN, GSTIN, bank details, invoices or confidential internal information into external AI tools or personal repositories, unless the company expressly approves it.
Check your contract before publishing anything; build on personal time and devices.
Type and understand code; don't copy AI output blindly. Predict the output before running it.
Stuck for 15 minutes? Ask for a hint, not a complete solution.
Never invent experience, titles or dates.
Never resign without a written offer.
Keep the plan manageable during go-live periods: use the reduced routine without guilt.
Recover after missed days by continuing in order, not by doubling up.
Protect health, sleep and family responsibilities. No streak is worth losing them.
No new subjects unless this plan is reviewed first.
Private GitHub repos; the app's signing key only in GitHub Secrets and your private Drive.

accountingQuestions.prompt: Who is personally liable, without limit, for a sole trader's debts?
accountingQuestions.explanation: A sole trader and the business are the same person in law.

accountingQuestions.prompt: A company's shareholders are liable for its debts…
options: Only up to the capital they put in
accountingQuestions.answer: Only up to the capital they put in
accountingQuestions.explanation: That's limited liability: the company is a separate legal person.

accountingQuestions.prompt: Which is a separate legal entity?
accountingQuestions.explanation: A company can own assets and be sued in its own name.

accountingQuestions.prompt: Ravi Traders' machinery is…
accountingQuestions.explanation: It's owned and used for years.

accountingQuestions.prompt: A bank loan Ravi Traders must repay is…
accountingQuestions.explanation: It's owed to someone else.

accountingQuestions.prompt: Sales of goods are…
accountingQuestions.explanation: Money earned by the business.

accountingQuestions.prompt: Rent paid for the shop is…
accountingQuestions.explanation: A cost of running the business.

accountingQuestions.prompt: In an accounting information system, a vendor invoice keyed into the ERP is the…
accountingQuestions.explanation: Input → process (checks, posting) → output (entries, reports).

accountingQuestions.prompt: A current asset is…
options: Stock you expect to sell this year
accountingQuestions.answer: Stock you expect to sell this year
accountingQuestions.explanation: Current means within about a year.

accountingQuestions.prompt: Where does a vendor's unpaid invoice appear?
accountingQuestions.explanation: You owe it soon, so it's a current liability.

accountingQuestions.prompt: Gross profit is…
options: Sales minus cost of goods sold
accountingQuestions.answer: Sales minus cost of goods sold
accountingQuestions.explanation: Net profit then subtracts the running expenses.

accountingQuestions.prompt: An expense is booked when…
accountingQuestions.explanation: That's the accrual principle.

accountingQuestions.prompt: Prudence (conservatism) means…
options: Use a new method every year
accountingQuestions.explanation: Expect losses; don't count gains before they happen.

accountingQuestions.prompt: Cash is which type of account?
accountingQuestions.explanation: Things you own (cash, furniture, goods) are real accounts.

accountingQuestions.prompt: A vendor is which type of account?
accountingQuestions.explanation: People and businesses are personal accounts.

accountingQuestions.prompt: Salaries are which type of account?
accountingQuestions.explanation: Expenses, losses, incomes and gains are nominal accounts.

accountingQuestions.prompt: Ravi Traders buys goods for ₹10,000 + 18% GST on credit. The entry is…
options: Dr Purchases 10,000 · Dr Input GST 1,800 · Cr Vendor 11,800
Dr Vendor 11,800 · Cr Purchases 10,000 · Cr Input GST 1,800
Dr Purchases 10,000 · Cr Vendor 10,000 · Cr Output GST 1,800
accountingQuestions.answer: Dr Purchases 10,000 · Dr Input GST 1,800 · Cr Vendor 11,800
accountingQuestions.explanation: GST paid on purchases is Input GST (a debit); the vendor is owed the total.

accountingQuestions.prompt: Ravi Traders sells goods for ₹20,000 + 18% GST on credit. The entry is…
options: Dr Customer 23,600 · Cr Sales 20,000 · Cr Output GST 3,600
Dr Sales 20,000 · Dr Output GST 3,600 · Cr Customer 23,600
accountingQuestions.answer: Dr Customer 23,600 · Cr Sales 20,000 · Cr Output GST 3,600
accountingQuestions.explanation: GST charged on sales is Output GST, a credit owed to the government.

accountingQuestions.prompt: Ravi Traders pays a vendor ₹9,800 in full settlement of ₹10,000. The entry is…
options: Dr Vendor 10,000 · Cr Bank 9,800 · Cr Discount received 200
Dr Vendor 10,000 · Dr Discount allowed 200 · Cr Bank 10,200
Dr Bank 9,800 · Dr Discount received 200 · Cr Vendor 10,000
accountingQuestions.answer: Dr Vendor 10,000 · Cr Bank 9,800 · Cr Discount received 200
accountingQuestions.explanation: The full debt is cleared; the ₹200 not paid is income.

accountingQuestions.prompt: After the journal, the next step is…
accountingQuestions.explanation: Journal → ledger → (in February) trial balance.

accountingQuestions.prompt: Why does Capital normally have a credit balance?
options: The business owes it to the owner
accountingQuestions.answer: The business owes it to the owner
accountingQuestions.explanation: Liabilities and capital sit on the credit side.
